newsitem.title: UK: Shell stock-split lifts investors' spirits.
newsitem.headline: Shell stock-split lifts investors' spirits.

text.p: Share splits and encouraging dividend pay-outs fired shares in Royal Dutch Petroleum and Shell Transport and Trading to 12 month highs.
But industry watchers failed to get overly excited about a 15 percent full-year profit rise for Royal Dutch/Shell Group.

"The fundamentals of this company remain the same. They have a good exploration and production story, some potential in refining and marketing and chemicals looks under the weather," said analyst Shawn Reynolds at Lehman Brothers.
Shell Group's full-year profit rose to 5.20 billion stg from 4.52 billion stg.
Fourth quarter earnings before exceptional items in exploration and production rose to 979 million stg from 508 million, helped by both higher production and oil prices.

The group, in which Royal Dutch holds 60 percent and Shell Transport the remainder, said oil and gas reserves had been replaced last year and added that output would grow by an annual seven percent in the years to 2001.

Shell, which like any other oil companies is suffering from overcapacity in the refining industry, said it expected to sign a letter of intent in the next few weeks on its planned U.S. downstream merger with Texaco.
Such a combination of operations could significantly help improve margins, but analysts reserve judgement until they have seen the details of the downstream link-up.
"It could go down really well in the market, but there are rumours we will see a merger in a very diluted form," said Reynolds.

Fourth-quarter group earnings in refining and marketing fell to 327 million stg from 346 million. In chemicals, earnings rose to 139 million stg from 54 million, mainly due to a signifivant improvement at the Montell Polyolefins unit.
But Shell said it expected chemicals markets to remain generally tough in 1997.
Royal Dutch said it would split its shares on a four-for-one basis, while Shell Transport is to issue two new shares for every one held.
Analysts cited this as the main reason for Royal Dutch shares to close 11.70 guilders higher at 347.50 in Amsterdam, while Shell Transport advanced 26 pence to 1,087-1/2.
Shell Transport was also boosted by a favourable final dividend 22.5 pence compared with 20.4 pence last year.
"Investors also took a bit comfort from the dividend because a few people were concerned that sterling growth might curtail Shell's dividend growth," said analyst Paul Spedding at Kleinwort Benson.
